title: Primitive Recursiveness of Counted Iteration
statement: Let $A$ be a type with a primitive recursive coding. Suppose $r$ assigns to each $a\in A$ a partial reader on finite Boolean strings, jointly primitive recursive in $a$ and the string, and let $\mathrm{count}:A\to\mathbb{N}$ be primitive recursive. Then the function that applies $r(a)$ to a string successively $\mathrm{count}(a)$ times, passing each resulting suffix to the next application and failing if any application fails, is jointly primitive recursive in $a$ and the string.
hypotheses_covered: $r:A\to\text{List Bool}\to\text{Option (List Bool)}$ is jointly primitive recursive
replaced:
Let $A$ be a type with a primitive recursive coding, let $r$ assign to each
$a \in A$ a partial reader on Boolean strings, primitive recursively jointly in $a$
and the string, and let $\mathrm{count} \colon A \to \bbn$ be primitive recursive.
Then the function taking $a$ and a string to the result of applying the reader
$r(a)$ sequentially $\mathrm{count}(a)$ times is primitive recursive jointly in $a$
and the string.
